body:
Correction. The "Readings" section of this pull request said that `--minimized` works. It does not work when a project is on the command line: the program stops with exit code 101 after the project loads. The tests in the "Testing" section do not cover this case.

Cause: a minimized window has no area, so egui lays out a 10000 x 10000 point screen, and the 3D target asks for a texture that is larger than the GPU limit. Details are in the comment on #3582.

`--no-activate` is not affected. I changed the description to say this. A fix with a test is in progress, and I will update this branch when it is ready. Please do not merge this pull request before that.
The fix for the `--minimized` crash is pushed (commit 061f78555). This pull request stays a draft.

Second read of head `061f78555` (read-only Opus agent, nothing built, the application was not started). This comment is not the review. The review of mkinney on this head stands.

**Result: no blocker.**

- **The exit 101.** A minimized window has no area, so egui uses its default screen of 10000 x 10000 points, and `fit_target` asked the device for a texture larger than its limit. The fix has two layers: `viewport_after_layout` keeps the last real viewport size when a side of the window is zero, and `limit_extent` in `fit_target` clamps each side to the device limit. The other places that use the size (surface configure at start and on resize, the aspect ratio, the MSAA and depth targets, the stock eye, the capture) already clamp to 1 or have a zero guard.
- **A window that is minimized later** has the same latent fault on `main`. This PR corrects it too, because the guard runs each frame.
- **The default start does not change.** The 264 deleted lines are a change of line ends in `cli_options.rs` (CRLF to LF). With no flag, `with_active` is true and `focus_window()` is called, as before.
- **Platforms.** `with_active`, `set_minimized` and `focus_window` are in winit on each desktop platform. The wasm shell only takes the new parameter. Wayland ignores `with_active`; the decision file says so. Linux and macOS were not tested.
- **Rules.** The `#[test]` count goes up by 7. No snapshot, no dependency, no document state. `git merge-tree` with main `f35202134` is clean, and also with #3585.

Notes, none is a blocker:

1. `shell_window.rs` goes from 397 to 405 lines, and `frame.rs` from 425 to 429. A split is a `P7` follow-up (together with the same note on #3585).
2. The doc comment of `limit_extent` says "Never zero", but a zero side passes through. The two callers clamp to 1.
3. The change of line ends in `cli_options.rs` makes each other open PR that edits that file conflict.

The trial merge on the current main (`camcraft-ui` lib, the integration suites, clippy; tests only) is in the queue. The merge follows a green trial.

Merge note. Class: no refresh (head `061f78555` merged unchanged). Basis: the review of mkinney on this head, the second read (no blocker), and the trial merge `99a393d10` on main `f35202134` (not pushed; tests only, the application was not started): `camcraft-ui` lib 1492 passed, 0 failed; all 23 integration binaries green; clippy `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` clean. Main moved after the trial by #2836 (sinker); `git merge-tree` with main `9e5af7b91` is clean. Linux and macOS behaviour of the two options was not tested. The follow-up for the file sizes is #3614.
